answer.rationale: Daily settlement peak is a recurring load condition; the release two hours ago is the only new variable, and write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes after that deploy. memory_b1 is the closest prior: rollback restored a stable checkout/write path without customer impact, which matches the objective of availability without losing writes. Enable_circuit_breaker is rejected because memory_b4’s fail-fast pattern would drop customer writes at peak settlement (downstream value risk). add_capacity (memory_b3) and route_read_replicas address load/read mix but not a release-induced write regression; regional failover has no regional signal. Uncertainty remains because peak and release are confounded and memory_b1 described an error spike, not latency—verify that record before committing. One window means the rollback must be fleet-wide to restore the write path.
